I'll bid $57 for SHORT_LINE. Mortgage it immediately to recover $100. That nets me $43 in cash. The bid stays below the $100 threshold where I drop out.

If I fold now, p2 wins at $56 and can mortgage SHORT_LINE for $100, netting $44. I should keep bidding to prevent that.

Bidding to $99 is the practical limit. p2 has $225 cash, but paying $100 would be break-even for them if they only want the mortgage value. I own two other mortgaged railroads, so owning SHORT_LINE would give me just one active railroad and $25 in rent.

Unmortgage costs $110 each. p2 owns B_O_RAILROAD mortgaged, so they would have one active railroad if they win SHORT_LINE. From WATER_WORKS, the next spaces are Marvin Gardens, Go to Jail, Pacific Avenue, North Carolina, Community Chest, Pennsylvania Avenue, and SHORT_LINE.

I'm now calculating the rent risk if I land on Park Place or Boardwalk. Both spaces have three houses, so rent would be $1,100 and $1,400 respectively. With only $546 cash, landing there would bankrupt me unless I can raise funds quickly.

I don't have a pink or yellow monopoly. States Avenue is unmortgaged with no houses, worth $70 to mortgage. I own four houses on Oriental Avenue and three on Vermont and Connecticut. p2 owns two mortgaged railroads.

I have a light blue monopoly with ten houses across Oriental, Vermont, and Connecticut. Selling all of them would raise $250. I cannot mortgage those properties while they still have houses, so I must sell the houses first.

Fully liquidating all properties yields $1,156. That covers the $1,100 rent on Park Place with $56 remaining, but it is still short of the $1,400 rent on Boardwalk. Liquidity is therefore critical for surviving a landing on Park Place.

Winning at $57 would raise my max liquid to $1,199. That still leaves a $99 gap against Park Place rent.

If I let p2 win at $56, their cash would jump from $225 to $269 after mortgaging the property. They gain $44 net.

Forcing them to $99 would only leave them with about $226 after mortgaging. Their net gain drops to roughly $1.

A $100 bid leaves p2 with $225 after mortgaging, so they break even. I will jump to $99 to end the auction quickly and minimize their cash gain. I need to make one tool call.

I will bid $99. If p2 matches, I drop out at $100 and deny them the arbitrage. They would break even after mortgaging. I cannot bid above $100.

p2 is currently on SHORT_LINE. They likely declined the $200 purchase price and are now bidding below that for the auction. Their maximum rational bid is probably well below $200.

I will keep bidding $57. The $100 mortgage and cash denial are the main value. Rent is low while my other railroads are mortgaged.

p2 owns an orange monopoly with four houses on every property. They also own an incomplete red monopoly with Kentucky and Illinois unmortgaged.

p2's red monopoly is incomplete because Indiana is mortgaged, so they cannot build there. Most of their properties are mortgaged and generate no rent. I am now calculating the exact orange monopoly rent values with four houses on each property.

The orange monopoly with four houses each yields $750 on St. James and Tennessee, and $800 on New York. Fully liquidating all assets leaves roughly $400 after St. James or Tennessee, but only about $356 after New York. I can survive those two spaces, though barely.

Four houses on the orange monopoly cost $750, and a hotel would be $950 or $1,000. Fully liquidating my assets still leaves enough cash to survive those amounts.

If p2 lands on my light blue properties with houses, I can hit them hard: three houses there yield $270, $270, and $300 in rent.

p2 could liquidate $1,425 by selling all houses and mortgaging properties. That covers the $450 rent on Oriental Avenue with houses.
